'''Nelly Vladimirovna Litvak''' ({{langx|ru|Нелли Владимировна Литвак}}, born January 27, 1972){{r|born}} is a Russian and Dutch [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] whose research includes the study of [[complex network]]s, [[stochastic process]]es, and their applications in [[medical logistics]]. Formerly a professor at the [[University of Twente]], she moved to the [[Eindhoven University of Technology]] in 2023.{{r|move}}

==Education and career==
Nelly Litvak was born in Gorky (now [[Nizhny Novgorod]]), Russia{{r|born}} to the journalist {{ill|Nina Zvereva (journalist)|lt=Nina Zvereva|ru|Зверева, Нина Витальевна}} and the researcher Vladimir Antonets.<ref name=niz>[https://ninazvereva.ru/family семья что надо], Nina Zvereva personal website</ref><ref>[https://www.names52.ru/alleyzoloto/tpost/vo07yrbju1-antonets-vladimir-aleksandrovich-i-zvere Антонец Владимир Александрович и Зверева Нина Витальевна]</ref> In 1995 Litvak graduated from the [[N. I. Lobachevsky State University of Nizhny Novgorod]],<ref>[https://www.utwente.nl/en/eemcs/sor/current-staff/litvak/cv/ Short CV]</ref> and in 1998 she earned the [[Candidate (degree)|candidate's degree in physical and mathematical sciences]] from the latter university with the dissertation ''Adaptive Control of Conflicting Flows'' supervised by Mikhail Andreevich Fedotkin.<ref>[https://www.dissercat.com/content/adaptivnoe-upravlenie-konfliktnymi-potokami Адаптивное управление конфликтными потоками] (''Adaptive Control of Conflicting Flows'')
:The subject of the thesis belongs to [[queueing theory]]. ''Quote:'' "Наиболее распространенным реальным примером системы с конфликтными потоками является перекресток, регулируемый светофором. <...> В данной работе будет изучен класс алгоритмов управления транспортом, где длительность зеленого света зависит от длины очереди и наличия поступлений по "зеленому" направлению, а порядок переключений при определенных условиях зависит от очередности подхода машин."</ref>  In 1999 she moved to the Netherlands.{{r|born}} She completed another doctoral degree in 2002, a Ph.D. from the Eindhoven University of Technology, with the dissertation ''Collecting <math>n</math> Items Randomly Located on a Circle'', completed in [[EURANDOM]],<ref>[https://pure.tue.nl/ws/portalfiles/portal/2160930/200210141.pdf Collecting n items randomly located on a circle]</ref> jointly [[ius promovendi|promoted]] by Ivo Adan, [[Jaap Wessels]], and [[Henk Zijm]].{{r|mg}}

She became a lecturer at the University of Twente in 2002, and was promoted to associate professor in 2011 and full professor in 2018. In 2017, she took on a second part-time affiliation with the Eindhoven University of Technology, and in 2023 she moved from Twente to a full-time position at the Eindhoven University of Technology,{{r|move}} as professor of algorithms for complex networks.{{r|tue}}

==Books==
Litvak is the author of several [[popular science]] books, including:
*''Наши хорошие подростки'' (''Our good teenagers'', in Russian, Alpina, 2010)
*''Формула призвания – 7 правил выбора вуза'' (''Vocation formula – 7 rules for choosing university'', Alpina, 2012)
*''IQ to Love: What makes highly intelligent men attractive to women'' (self-published, 2014)
*''Кому нужна математика? Понятная книга о том, как устроен цифровой мир'' (''{{ill|Who Needs Mathematics?|ru|Кому нужна математика?}} A Clear Book about how the Digital World Works'', with {{ill|Andrey Raygorodsky|ru|Райгородский, Андрей Михайлович}}, in Russian, Mann-Ivanov-Ferber («Манн, Иванов и Фербер»), 2017)
**The book was shortlisted for the Russian 2017 [[Enlightener Prize]].<ref>Юлия Гусарова. [https://snob.ru/entry/152790/ Дотракийский язык, депрессия горожан и ложь в интернете. О чем книги номинантов на премию «Просветитель»], October 6, 2017, {{ill|Snob Magazine|ru|Сноб (журнал)}}</ref> 
*''Математика для безнадежных гуманитариев'' (''Mathematics for hopeless humanities geeks'', with Alla Kechedzhan, in Russian, AST, 2019)

==Recognition==
Litvak was awarded the 2002 [[Thomas Joannes Stieltjes|Stieltjes]] Prize for her Ph.D. dissertation.<ref>[https://stieltjes.org/stieltjes/stielprijs.php Stieltjes Prize]</ref> She was the 2011 recipient of the Professor De Winter award of the University of Twente, given annually to recognize the research of a female faculty member.{{r|dewinter}} She was named the university's teacher of the year in 2022.{{r|toy}}

==Personal==
While in the Netherlands, Nelly Litvak married to Pranab Mandal.<ref name=dida>Diana Dalenoord, [https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/pranab-mandal-international-programme-director-plans-diana-dalenoord Pranab Mandal, the international programme director of Applied Mathematics with plans]</ref> She has two daughters: Natalia (born in 1993 from the first marriage<ref name=niz/>) and Piyali (born in 2005 to Nelly and Pranab).{{r|born}} She has younger sister Yekaterina and brother Pyotr.<ref>Introduction in: ''Наши хорошие подростки'' (''Our good teenagers'', in Russian, Alpina, 2010)</ref><ref name=niz/>
